title: Counting the sky
intro: People kept tallies long before they kept words. A notched bone, a row of scratches, a count of moons: the first measurements were marks made to remember how many.
Later, those who watched the sky found that its changes repeated, and a count could predict the next one.
handoff: Counting gave later thinkers numbers to argue with.
diagramLabel: Tally marks resolving into a lunar cycle

lines.title: Notches on the Ishango bone
lines.summary: A bone carved with grouped notches may be the oldest surviving record of counting.
lines.replaced: The idea that quantity could only be held in memory.
lines.enabled: Written number systems and, much later, arithmetic as a craft.

lines.title: The Plimpton 322 tablet
lines.summary: A Babylonian clay tablet lists number triples that fit right-angled triangles.
lines.replaced: Geometry as a matter of measuring one field at a time.
lines.enabled: General rules for lengths, later proved by Greek mathematicians.

title: Giving reasons
intro: Greek thinkers asked why a rule holds, not only that it does. A proof replaced a recipe.
That habit gave later astronomers and physicians a standard to meet.
handoff: Proof became the standard for knowing.
diagramLabel: A circle inscribed in a square

lines.title: Thales asks for natural causes
lines.summary: Thales explains earthquakes by water, not gods, and sets the form of the question.
lines.replaced: Myth as the default account of nature.
lines.enabled: Natural philosophy as a tradition of argument.

lines.title: Euclid's Elements
lines.summary: Thirteen books build geometry from a few axioms by deduction alone.
lines.replaced: Collections of separate rules with no common base.
lines.enabled: The model of a science built from stated assumptions.

title: Trying it and seeing
intro: Scholars began to test claims by experiment. Ibn al-Haytham did it with light.
A claim now had to survive a trial, and the trial had to be described.
handoff: Experiment became a way to settle arguments.

lines.title: Ibn al-Haytham's Book of Optics
lines.summary: Seven books combine geometry and experiment to show that we see by light entering the eye.
lines.replaced: The view that the eye sends out rays.
lines.enabled: Experimental method in physics and the camera obscura.

lines.title: Kepler's ellipses
lines.summary: Planets move on ellipses, a result drawn from Tycho Brahe's precise observations.
